vermagicProvenance.method: first occurrence of the ' SMP preempt mod_unload modversions aarch64' tail, scanned back to the first non-printable byte (same rule as ir-loader/tests/loader_contract.py:kernel_vermagic)

addressSpace.note: the symbol list starts _text at offset 0, i.e. offsets are image-relative; __start_BTF landing exactly on the .BTF magic byte proves the two spaces coincide for this image

btf.provenance: image .BTF at 0x16d1b50, parsed with the kernel's own BTF encoding (kernel/bpf/btf.c); every type id below is a BTF id

bssBlindSpot.why: the list is built from the image *file*. .bss is a NOLOAD section: it occupies no file bytes, so every .bss symbol's address is at or past the end of the file and it cannot appear in the list. The declaration is checkable: the highest listed symbol sits 0x1f8 bytes before EOF, and .bss is page aligned, so .bss starts at the first page at or after that point.
bssBlindSpot.consequence: absence from this list clears function names (all of .text is inside the file) but never data names; a data object missing from the list must be verified on the device, not inferred absent

symbolListCoverage.note: counts are over names, not rows: kallsyms can carry several entries for one name
symbolListCoverage.improvement: the shipped list drops every symbol whose address is at or past the end of the image file. Regenerate it without that filter (keep out-of-file addresses) and this contract's data-name verdicts stop being 'unverified' and become present/absent, because .bss would then be represented

kprobe.note: register_kprobe() fills addr from symbol_name; the module zeroes the whole object first, so the leading bookkeeping fields (hlist/list/nmissed) never matter

varInBtf.note: not probative: this BTF encodes almost no variables (a few hundred VARs against tens of thousands of objects), so a missing VAR says nothing about the symbol

selinuxState.writtenByModule: enforcing = 0, restored on every failure path and in cleanup_module

subprocessInfo.writtenByModule: path only: setup() replaces it with the empty CONFIG_STATIC_USERMODEHELPER_PATH string, and the module writes the helper path back before exec()
subprocessInfo.readBy: call_usermodehelper_exec() reads path (ldr x8,[x19,#0x38]; ldrb w8,[x8]) and returns 0 immediately when the first byte is NUL

kretprobe.note: kp@+0x0 is a struct kprobe, so the surrogate the module declares must be at least 0xb0 bytes: the kernel writes the whole object, including freelist/rph past data_size. handler and entry_handler share one type (kretprobe_handler_t)

ptRegs.note: syscallno is at 0x118, not at the end of the embedded user_pt_regs (0x110): orig_x0 occupies 0x110. The module reads regs->syscallno, never a per-release offset

kernelParam.note: the glue writes one row of this struct by hand (C1-6), so the offsets must come from here, not from a hand-copied header

exportTable.method: a symbol's export class is the range its __ksymtab_<name> entry address falls in; both bounds are the kernel's own linker symbols, so no heuristic is involved

site.note: clang kCFI builds the expected type hash for `int (void)` in w17, compares it with the callee's 4-byte prefix and traps on mismatch before the indirect call; a module's init_module must therefore begin with this 32-bit value

licenseRationale.why: a non-GPL module may not resolve a symbol whose __ksymtab entry lives in __ksymtab_gpl, so register_kprobe() alone forces license=GPL; nothing else about this module is GPL-specific

declarationCheck.why: clang's KCFI type id is a hash of the function type, and a pointer to a struct contributes the *record name*. Two otherwise identical prototypes that differ only in the struct name therefore get different ids, so a callback declared with a shim struct name would compare against the wrong id and trap on its first call. That is the whole reason L2 callback prototypes must use the kernel's struct names.
declarationCheck.method: compile one TU per case with the repo's L2 flag set, read the 4 bytes before the callback's entry point (that is the __cfi_ prefix clang emits), and compare with the image's compare-site id

declarationCheck.note: no_sanitize("kcfi") on the callee does not remove the prefix (measured on this toolchain), so G8's 'callback keeps its prefix' rule must be a source/attribute check, not a prefix test

l2.importKcfiRule: none of the six carries a KCFI type signature. The 4 bytes before each entry point (recorded per import as kcfiPrefix) are not one of the type ids any compare site in this image builds, i.e. the function has no __cfi_ prefix. An indirect call to it from a *sanitised* function therefore compares garbage against garbage and takes brk #0x8228, which is a panic under CONFIG_PANIC_ON_OOPS=y. An import goes through the PLT with no type check at all, which is why these six are imports and only the three unexported names below are runtime lookups. This is the reverse direction of the __nocfi asymmetry used by the root module (callers of *resolved* pointers are __nocfi; callbacks invoked *by* the kernel keep their prefix).

cookieChannel.why: the cookie arrives from the loader only: finit_module's uargs are supplied by the process that loads the module (the helper, inside the window), so no other process can know it and OP_ARM can require cookie == l2.load_cookie instead of accepting whoever calls first (R-L2-14)
cookieChannel.failureSemantics: a missing or zero cookie makes init_module return -EINVAL (nothing is armed) and the helper records MA_L2_NO_COOKIE; a zero-cookie module that somehow loads refuses every ARM with -EPERM
cookieChannel.notExercised: NOT_EXERCISED on device: neither __param nor finit_module uargs has ever run on this hardware (design §7.3)

controlAbi.freeze: design §3.1.2 (op table) and its calling convention; L3 reuses the same channel and may not re-assign the registers
controlAbi.carrier: __arm64_sys_ni_syscall, reached only through an unimplemented syscall number
controlAbi.call: syscall(scno, op, a1, a2, a3, x5=result, x6=0, x7=cookie)

registers.x0: scno (the kernel proves it from pt_regs->syscallno, not from the caller's claim)
registers.x5: user pointer to the 32-byte result block (0 = no result wanted)
registers.x6: reserved, must be 0 (a non-zero value is refused, which leaves room for an old kernel to reject a newer call)
registers.x7: cookie (64-bit; written into the kernel by OP_ARM, which requires the value the helper injected through finit_module uargs at load time)

controlAbi.returns: -ENOSYS always (the carrier's real return; the module never rewrites the syscall return value)

kcfiIdChecks.note: a mismatch means the pinned id is not the id this image compares at the anchor function's dispatch site: the id must be re-measured before any module is built against it

handover.why: the helper execs the long-lived consumer and never exits, so WAIT_PROC would park init_module() in kernel_wait() while holding module_mutex
handover.returnZeroIsNotProof: the helper's own side effect (provider-log line plus a `getenforce` readback) is the only proof the handover happened; init_module's return value and its printks are not, because the four-argument wrapper returns 0 silently on this image
handover.cleanupModule: defined; it is this_module.exit and the only in-kernel restore point reachable through delete_module()

sequence: info = setup(helper, argv, envp, GFP_KERNEL, NULL, NULL, NULL)
primaryPath.why: setup() overwrites the caller's path with the empty CONFIG_STATIC_USERMODEHELPER_PATH string; restoring it at subprocess_info.path is the whole fix (DirtyFragX lkm/dfroot.c:185-188 does the same on this device family)

fallback.usedOnlyWhen: setup or exec cannot be resolved
fallback.logged: maplesu_root: umh setup/exec unresolved (setup=%px exec=%px); falling back to the four-argument wrapper
fallback.why: it keeps the import set at exactly four and the module loadable on a kernel where the pair is missing, but on this static-UMH image it cannot exec anything: it returns 0 and the module must not treat that as proof

helperArgv.savedValue: the enforcement byte init_module() read before it wrote 0 ('0' or '1', the value its `selinux permissive for handover (was %d) own_window=%d` printk names). Step-4 (D4-4) adds the honesty field: own_window=1 means this module moved the byte and cleanup_module() must put it back; own_window=0 means the window was already open, the saved byte is inherited, and the module writes nothing back

storage.kind: file-scope static (.bss), never a stack local
storage.why: UMH_WAIT_EXEC returns when the exec succeeds; a stack block would be read after init_module() is gone (the reference dfroot.c uses static storage for the same reason)

originMapping.enforce_before==1: KERNEL_SAVED (source=kernel; the value is the kernel's own live byte, never written by the helper)
originMapping.enforce_before==0 && expected in {0,1}: BASELINE (source copied from the env: observed or baseline)

entryBaseline.whoWrites: App (DirtyfragAttempt.start, after publishConfig and before the provider starts; 0600, one line, <=192 bytes)
entryBaseline.whoReads: helper step 3.5 (hook_read_env, openat(dirfd), once, inside the window)
entryBaseline.why: the module loads after dfroot already wrote 0, so it cannot know the entry value; the App cannot read selinuxfs either, so it reports a *target plus provenance* rather than an observation. KERNEL_SAVED is reserved for the one case where the kernel's value is its own
entryBaseline.residualRisk: the env file is unauthenticated: the App owns it and could ask for expected=0/source=observed, leaving the device permissive until the next boot. It gains no capability it did not have, and DAEMON_READY is still refused because F1 requires restoreEnforcing==1

restoreOrder.why: the module's cleanup_module() runs inside delete_module() and writes back the byte it saved. Writing before the unload is therefore overwritten - which is exactly how step-3 produced wrote=1/readback_pre=0 while the device was still permissive. Restore-last makes the helper's write the final privileged action, and the unload child the only writer, so there is no second write and no swing back
restoreOrder.singleWriter: hook_unload_child only; the parent never writes
restoreOrder.preexisting: post_unload==want is logged as `restore preexisting=%d by=external` and NOT rewritten
restoreOrder.pendingMeans: the parent's bounded wait expired while the child is still retrying; PENDING is an expected outcome (R12's mitigation is the parent exiting so init_module returns and releases module_mutex), not a failure

failureReturns.-ENOSYS: kallsyms_lookup_name (or the kprobe that yields it) could not be resolved; nothing was read, written or restored
failureReturns.-ENOENT: selinux_state could not be resolved; the enforcement byte was never saved or changed, nothing was restored
failureReturns.-EINVAL: call_usermodehelper_setup/_exec could not both be resolved, so the four-argument fallback is the only path left - and on this static-UMH kernel that path cannot exec anything; the saved enforcing value was restored and nothing ran
failureReturns.-ENOMEM: call_usermodehelper_setup() returned NULL; nothing was queued, the saved enforcing value was restored
failureReturns.-ENODEV: call_usermodehelper_exec() returned non-zero, i.e. the helper was not exec'd ('nothing ran'); the saved enforcing value was restored

failureReturnsAppMapping.note: the override only fires when the module's own classified printk is in the dump taken for this failure; an empty or unreadable dump leaves the loader-layer token in place, so a missing kernel channel is never reported as a specific cause
